CFTC REPORTS @ 2:30 PM
MARKET HEADLINES
• Quick Editorial: volume and volatility slowed a bit overnight as the grains
coast into the end of the week, still very near fresh fund-fueled move highs as
the trade waits for those specific positions from the CFTC this afternoon, and
revised fundamental data from the USDA, StoneX, and others next week. It
appears the warm and sometimes-wet Midwest weather pattern will continue
right up into early harvest, beneficial for some of the U.S. crop but continually wearing on the rest as condition ratings mostly decline through the season.
• China’s Sinograin announced that they will auction off another 68k tonnes of
imported soybeans next Wednesday (September 9).
• FranceAgriMer reported another one-point decline in French corn condition
ratings this week, now to just 27% good/excellent, down from 62% a year
ago. Harvest of the crop was initially pegged at 3% complete, up from 0% last
year and the 1% five-year average. The country’s Ag Minister announced an
aid plan worth more than a billion euros to help the farming sector after this
year’s drought, while also estimating that 30-35k of France’s farms would be
at risk after the brutal growing season.
• Russia’s Ag Ministry reported the country’s grain harvest at more than 110
MMT so far, including 83.5 MMT of wheat.

WEATHER UPDATE
• Rains fell in the northern and northeastern Midwest over the past 24 hours,
holding in WI and MI this morning; an active pattern remains in the northern
Plains and belt over the next five days, drier in the southern half of the Midwest. The same overall precipitation pattern lingers long-term, with a wet
western U.S. creeping into the Plains and NW belt through mid-September,
and drier overall conditions in the central and eastern belt. Temperatures remain warm for at least the next two weeks.

• Argentine forecasts remain dry near-term but wetter overall conditions are
now seen later in the 6-10 day time frame to aid wheat moisture; Brazil was
dry over the past 24 hours but better rains will arrive in the north through early next week and center-south for the 6-10 day, aiding wheat moisture supplies and boosting soil moisture heading into the early planting time slot.
FUNDAMENTAL UPDATE
New-crop (still 2026/27, as weekly export sales reporting
still only goes to August 27) corn export sales beat expectations at 1.986 million tonnes (78 mbu) this week, though a
good chunk of that came from net OC cancellations rolled
into the next MY; cumulative sales of 14.444 MMT (569
mbu) remain behind LY, though ahead of the three before
that. Mexico remains easily the leading buyer at 5.163
MMT (203 mbu), followed by Japan at 2.3 MMT (91 mbu)
